s1.syndrome_frame: obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn
key_facts: 36 weeks' gestation pregnancy
Suspected fetal renal anomalies
Prenatal ultrasound showed bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis
Fetal bladder was markedly dilated
Left perirenal fluid collection measured 64 × 34 mm
Collection contained multiple light bands, flocculent echoes, and slightly echogenic material
Oligohydramnios present
Emergency cesarean delivery
Male infant with stable vital signs and normal physical examination
Elevated serum creatinine at 156.1 µmol/L
Postnatal MRI showed mixed T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands in the left perirenal collection
Magnetic resonance urography revealed bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention

shortlist.label: Posterior urethral valves
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, and postnatal MRI showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening

shortlist.label: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis

shortlist.label: Prune belly syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, and postnatal MRI showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening

shortlist.label: Urinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Left perirenal fluid collection with mixed T1 and T2 signals on postnatal MRI, consistent with urinoma

shortlist.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
shortlist.why_kept: Prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, and postnatal MRI showing mixed T1 and T2 signals in the left perirenal collection

raw.rationale: The prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a markedly dilated fetal bladder, and oligohydramnios, along with the postnatal MRI and magnetic resonance urography results showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention, are consistent with the diagnosis of posterior urethral valves, which is a common cause of obstructive uropathy in male infants.

rejected.label: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with unilateral hydronephrosis, which does not match the bilateral involvement seen in this case.

rejected.label: Prune belly syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by the absence of abdominal muscles, which was not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Urinoma
rejected.why: While a urinoma is present, it is likely a secondary finding due to the underlying obstructive uropathy, rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a non-functional kidney replaced by multiple cysts, which does not match the imaging findings in this case.
